doc.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999

title: Leaving Louis before 'High Society' and his 27 bags
summary: He quit Louis' band from travel fatigue and missed 'High Society'; stolen luggage and Louis' 27 bags.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: I know that he was very distressed about that. I would have been too. It’s like with me with Louis, I did the “Glenn Miller Story” but then when I left the band after traveling so much. One week we came from Norway or something and we went to Honolulu then we came back to Massachusetts and then they were going to Japan. I said, “I can’t make it,” I quit, I gave my notice. And I said I’m disturbed with Joe Glaser because he knew they were going to make “High Society,” and he didn’t say to me, “well why don’t you hang in there because we’re going to make—” so they made “High Society” and I don’t want to look at that movie because I should have been on that movie. Because I gave my notice because we were doing so many big jumps: Europe, Hawaii, back and forth. I got so tired.
I don’t know how Louis did it. He loved it.

He just loved it. He loved being on the road more than he did living at home. He carried everything with him, anything he owned. He had 27 bags on the road. Yeah, we got off a plane once and we were waiting for a bus to take us to Carolina or something, and they stole my bag. I had a big clothes — my big luggage, Samsonite, I had a big Samsonite. And it was on the sidewalk with a thousand pieces of luggage. So some guy came and says, I think it might have been the red cap or something, “man how many guys in your band?” We said, “six guys.” He said four thousand pieces of luggage! Well 27 are Louis’. He said 27? He carried everything on the road. And then I think we went to Georgia and when we got there my bag wasn’t there, I lost my bag. Somebody just picked it up, there was a million bags, easy, right? Just grab one and walk away. That’s what they did. So to get back to, where were we, with Krupa?
